post.summary:
Handles the Stripe SPI `authorize` request. Returns 200 with
`result.type = redirect_to_url` on success, 200 with `result.type = declined`
on resolver miss / merchant misconfig, 400 on malformed payload, 409 on a concurrent
retry with the same `payauthz_*` id.

Handles the Stripe SPI `cancel` request. Returns 204 on success, 400 on malformed
payload, 401 on signature/auth failure, 409 on a concurrent retry with the same id.

Handles the Stripe SPI `account_review` request sent during merchant onboarding and on
subsequent business-information changes (UMPS-574 / UMPS-582). Zip parses the review payload
and acknowledges receipt with `204 No Content` (no body); review processing is handled
out of band. Returns 409 on a concurrent retry with the same review id. Malformed-body (400),
signature (401) and payload-size (413) rejections are handled upstream by
`StripeSpiMiddleware` before MVC.

get.summary:
Browser-facing customer-cancel intercept (UMPS-353). Stripe's checkout sends the buyer
here on cancel; we dispatch Zip.Gateway.StripeDirect.Models.CheckoutCancelRequest to fire a best-effort
`buyer_abandoned` decline against Stripe's Financial Partner API and resolve the
merchant return_url from the persisted OrderContext, then 302 the browser there. Bypasses
`StripeSpiMiddleware` via the `/stripe-direct/v1/checkout` path-prefix exclusion
(no SPI signature on a browser GET).
            
The redirect target is resolved server-side only; this endpoint deliberately does NOT read
a return_url from the query string. Honoring a client-supplied URL would be an open redirect
usable for social-engineering / credential-phishing attacks.

post.summary:
Handles the Stripe SPI `refund` request (UMPS-354 decline + UMPS-355 approve). Returns
200 with `result.type = approved` when Zip refunds the customer, 200 with
`result.type = declined` on a sync decline, 400 when the order state can't be verified
(Stripe retries), 409 on a concurrent retry with the same `refauthz_*` id.

Handles the Stripe SPI `capture` notification. Stripe posts here when a merchant
captures the PaymentIntent for an authorization Zip approved. The capture is a notification,
not a request for permission — Zip always responds `204 No Content` and performs the
capture internally. Stripe retries on a non-204 with exponential back-off for up to 7 days.

Handles the Stripe SPI `settle` request (UMPS-628). Durably records a technical
receipt and hands the settlement off to Merchant Invoicing, then returns 204 immediately.
400 on malformed payload, 409 on a concurrent retry with the same `fpinvoice_*` id,
5xx when the receipt or handoff could not be recorded (Stripe retries for up to 7 days).

QuadPay.Gateway.StripeDirect.Models.Echo.description:
Failure envelope for `POST /internal/stripe-direct/echo` when Stripe returns
a non-success status. Surfaces Stripe's own status code + error code so failure
attribution is unambiguous — a bare gateway 500 would mask the upstream boundary
and send the on-call person down the wrong rabbit hole.

Success envelope for `POST /internal/stripe-direct/echo`. Carries both the
timestamp sent and the timestamp returned by Stripe so a runbook operator can see
the parity explicitly via QuadPay.Gateway.StripeDirect.Models.EchoConnectivityResult.Matched rather than having to compare two
numbers themselves.
